name: Pressure Field
description: Flow induction by pressure gradients. Drives hydraulic and pneumatic computation in biological and physical systems — from plant vascular transport to ocean currents to atmospheric dynamics. Follows minimum-path principles.

scope.definition: Pressure transmission uniformity in incompressible fluid — fractional variation of applied pressure across all points in a sealed fluid volume, measured in hydraulic actuator systems.

evidence.source: Pascal (1663) 'Traité de l'Equilibre des Liqueurs' (posthumous 1663); modern validation in ISO 4413:2010 hydraulic standard.
cross_domain_examples: hydraulic press: pressure uniform to ±0.01% across 1000 L fluid volume — Pascal's law validated
blood pressure transmission: arterial pulse travels at 5-8 m/s — near-instantaneous at organ scale
hydraulic brake system: 0.99 force multiplication efficiency from pedal to caliper
hydrostatic pressure in deep ocean: uniform to 0.1% at 10 km depth — gravitational correction only

scope.falsifiability: If pressure measurements at different points in a sealed incompressible fluid system show >0.5% variance after correcting for gravity, Pascal's principle is violated.
scope.measurement_limits: Deviations occur with compressible fluids (gases) and at very high pressures where fluid density changes measurably. Perfect Pascal's law requires ideal incompressibility — water deviates 0.004%/bar.
